difference: Code-point divergence: Korea signals data-only services with serviceCategory 10 (national value) whereas ATSC later assigned 7 (Data Service) and 8 (Common Data Service); Korea keeps 5 (EAS service) which ATSC deprecated; Korea lacks urlType 4 and OtherBsid, and adds SimulcastServiceInfo/serviceReceptionType.
impact: A receiver following A/331:2026 would not recognise Korean data-only services (10) as data services; Korean datacasting receivers key on value 10.
recommendation: Record the Korean values in the ATSC Code Point Registry or align Part 3 with serviceCategory 7/8 at the next revision.

ATSC.value: AEAT@aeaTableId; AEA @aeaId @issuer @audience @subAudience @aeaType @refAEAId @priority @category @wakeup; Header (@effective @expires EventCode EventDesc Location); AEAText; LiveMedia; Media (@mediaType …)

TTA.value: AEA-MF per the 2017 edition: no @aeaTableId, @subAudience, @category; adds <AEAVoiceText> (speech-friendly text, Korean addition); dateTime UTC written as '-00:00'. National usage (0142/R4): @issuer = broadcaster or originating agency (기상청·행정안전부·과학기술정보통신부), @audience 'public' baseline, EventCode/@type from national code tables (부속서 A), Location from 행정동 geocode or GPS circle (부속서 B), device codes (부속서 B-2), priority tied to mandatory-broadcast rules

SBTVD.value: AEAT generated by converting CAP 1.2 alerts: @wakeup = true only when priority is maximum; EventCode = COBRADE code (6 digits) with EventCode@type='COBRADE'; Location@type 'polygon' (IDAP alerts) or 'ZIP_BR'; broadcasters monitor the IDAP CAP feed (idapfile.mi.gov.br)

difference: The AEA-MF core is common. Korea's text predates A/331's @category/@subAudience/@aeaTableId and Media@mediaType, and adds AEAVoiceText; Korea defines national EventCode/Location/device code tables and issuer conventions. Brazil derives AEAT from CAP (IDAP) with COBRADE event codes and Brazilian location types, and ties wake-up to maximum priority.
impact: Receivers must apply national code tables (Korea) or COBRADE/ZIP_BR semantics (Brazil); alert content is not portable across countries even though the XML container is.
